confirmed.title: Product schema sin offers: los 3 productos no son elegibles para rich results de producto
confirmed.evidence:
Verificado en vivo (curl, HTTP 200, sin captcha) y en rendered-gluckbags-com-producto-1.html. El bloque JSON-LD de Product tiene solo estas claves: ['@context','@type','name','url','brand','description','image','category']. NO existe la propiedad `offers`. JSON real: [{"@type":"Product","name":"Tote Cognac","url":"https://gluckbags.com/producto/1","brand":{"@type":"Brand","name":"GLÜCK"},"description":"Tote Cognac — GLÜCK...","image":["https://gluckbags.com/media/products/1/.../787.jpg"],"category":"Tote"}] Google exige `offers` (o `review`/`aggregateRating`) para que un Product genere cualquier rich result; sin ninguno de los tres, Search Console lo marca como inválido para resultados enriquecidos. Matiz importante: la PDP no muestra precio — el precio visible es el texto 'Consultar' (

Consultar

) y el CTA es 'Consultar por Instagram'. Es un catálogo/lookbook sin checkout.
confirmed.recommendation: Decidir el modelado según el negocio: (a) si se quiere elegibilidad de producto, agregar `offers` con `priceCurrency: ARS`, un `price` (o `priceSpecification`) y `availability` (https://schema.org/InStock); como no hay precio público, lo correcto es publicar el precio o usar `offers.availability` + `offers.url` apuntando al canal de venta (Instagram) — Google no acepta precios placeholder ni 0 ficticio. (b) Si la decisión es no exponer precio, retirar el @type Product (que promete commerce) y modelarlo como `ItemPage`/`CreativeWork` o solo `BreadcrumbList`, para no declarar un Product incompleto que Search Console reportará como error. Mantener consistencia con el contenido visible ('Consultar').
confirmed.verifyNotes:
CONFIRMED live (browser UA, HTTP 200, no sg-captcha) and in artifacts. The Product JSON-LD on every PDP lacks offers/review/aggregateRating. Independent reproduction: - LIVE curl https://gluckbags.com/producto/1, /2, /4 -> HTTP 200, no captcha. Each emits exactly one Product JSON-LD with keys ['@context','@type','name','url','brand','description','image','category']. offers=False, review=False, aggregateRating=False on all three. (Spot-checked 1/2/4; pattern is identical and template-driven.) - Artifacts (artifacts/rendered-gluckbags-com-producto-1.html, -2, -3) match exactly: same 8 keys, none of the 3 required eligibility properties. BreadcrumbList JSON-LD is also present and valid. - Price nuance verified live AND in artifacts:

Consultar

on all PDPs; CTA "Consultar por Instagram" present. No price, no checkout — it is a lookbook/catalog. - Scope verified: sitemap-urls.json + all-urls.txt list /producto/1..5; live /producto/4 returns 200 with the same defective schema, so the issue spans all 5 product URLs, not just the 3 sampled. Technical claim is 100% accurate: Google's Product rich-result guidelines require offers OR review OR aggregateRating; with none, Search Console flags an error ("Either 'offers', 'review', or 'aggregateRating' should be specified") and the page earns no product rich result. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED high -> medium. Rationale: it IS a real, reproducible rich-result eligibility error worth fixing, but business context caps the upside. With genuinely no price (Consultar), the site cannot honestly add offers (offers needs price/priceCurrency), so the only honest fix paths are review/aggregateRating (no reviews exist today) or removing the Product type. The lost opportunity is product rich snippets on 5 thin, non-transactional catalog pages with no checkout intent — not a traffic-threatening defect. Practical remediation: either drop @type Product (use a simpler type) to clear the SC error, or add aggregateRating/review once real reviews exist. Not a false positive, not stale, not intentional-noindex, not a captcha artifact.

confirmed.title: Product schema sin identificadores ni señales de confianza recomendadas (sku/gtin/mpn, aggregateRating, review)

Organization con "@id":"https://gluckbags.com/#org" y en el Product "brand":{"@id":"https://gluckbags.com/#org"}). Si en algún momento hay reseñas reales (no inventadas), sumar `aggregateRating`/`review` — nunca markup que no corresponda a contenido visible (riesgo de spam/penalización).

Tote

confirmed.title: BreadcrumbList de las PDP no coincide con el breadcrumb visible de la página

Tote

Tote Cognac

confirmed.title: Organization de la home demasiado genérica para un e-commerce: sin tipo específico ni contactPoint, y desaprovecha sameAs

La home declara Organization con claves ['@context','@type','name','url','logo','sameAs'] y sameAs=["https://www.instagram.com/gluck_bags/"], y un WebSite con solo ['@context','@type','name','url'] (sin potentialAction — correcto, porque el ?s= no es una búsqueda real: /?s=seo devuelve la home con canonical a / ). El logo https://gluckbags.com/static/img/marca/avatar-perfil-gluck.jpg responde 200 (image/jpeg, 10.5 KB). Como es una tienda de carteras, `Organization` a secas pierde matices: no hay `OnlineStore`/`Brand` consolidado, ni `contactPoint`. La página /contacto aún tiene los datos en placeholder ('WhatsApp: (a completar)', 'Email: (a completar)'), por eso un ContactPoint todavía no es markup justificable.
confirmed.recommendation: Considerar especializar el @type a `OnlineStore` (subtipo de Organization, soportado por Google) y darle un @id estable para vincularlo desde el `brand` de los productos. Mantener WebSite SIN SearchAction mientras no exista una búsqueda interna real (agregarla ahora sería markup que no matchea una feature → riesgo). Cuando /contacto tenga email/WhatsApp reales (hoy son placeholders), recién ahí sumar `contactPoint` con esos canales.
confirmed.verifyNotes:
CONFIRMED on the live site (HTTP 200, no sg-captcha) and in artifacts (raw + rendered HTML), so it is server-rendered, not JS-only or a throttling artifact.

Live home JSON-LD (curl, browser UA) is exactly two blocks:
- Organization: keys ['@context','@type','name','url','logo','sameAs']; @type just "Organization" (no OnlineStore/Brand), no contactPoint; sameAs = ["https://www.instagram.com/gluck_bags/"] (Instagram only).
- WebSite: keys ['@context','@type','name','url'] only — no potentialAction/SearchAction.
Logo https://gluckbags.com/static/img/marca/avatar-perfil-gluck.jpg → HTTP/2 200, content-type image/jpeg, content-length 10534 (10.5 KB), as claimed.
Live /contacto (HTTP 200) still shows "a completar" placeholders for WhatsApp/Email, so the finding's reasoning that a ContactPoint is not yet justifiable holds. Absence of potentialAction is also reasonable since there is no real site search.

Severity kept at LOW (could even be info). This is an enhancement/quality observation, not a defect: the Organization markup is valid, not penalized, no false positive, no broken/erroneous markup. Adopting a more specific type (OnlineStore/Brand) and enriching sameAs are nice-to-haves for entity understanding, not rich-result blockers. The finding is appropriately self-restrained (it argues AGAINST adding contactPoint/SearchAction now), which is correct.

One inaccuracy in the evidence text, non-load-bearing: the finding says "/?s=seo ... canonical a /", but artifact seo-home-s-seo.json shows that page's canonical = https://gluck.nexttech.com.ar/ (the separate, already-known SITE_URL alias misconfig), not literally "/". confirmed.title: Páginas de producto sin contenido descriptivo único y Product schema sin offers (precio/disponibilidad)

Recommend adding unique per-product descriptive copy (materials/dimensions/care) on-page and in JSON-LD; add offers/availability only if/when prices are published.
